mechanisms: Builders stand in a plant's exit lane while they build beside it, and the player's only lever is to drop the build: armnanotc_2761, armnanotc_22524, armnanotc_27106 and armbeamer_30104 (510 metal, frames at 39-74% whose builders were 20-40 s from done); a build position outside the lane, or a lever that steps the builder out and keeps the build, would have kept all four.

No guard where the frame stood when raiders came: armnanotc_26291 and armadvsol_29628 in the 13:11-14:06 home raid (six Pawns in B5/B6, the picket away, a listed builder's next step ordered 660 from them) and armmex_4975 and armmex_12981 at D6 (136 metal); a guard kept at the base and at D6, and a list step held while a party is within reach of its site, would have kept most of it.

The hands began builds the player then had to drop, and both frames started inside the 7 s think penalty so the stop met a frame the player had not seen: the bare 'armadvsol' step placed by spot_99 with its builder in plant_13578's exit lane (armadvsol_25660) and the pick's second advanced plant a second after the first stood (armavp_25896), with armllt_14630 (an old list's engine-queued Sentry that started as the replacement list dropped it) (75 metal); placement out of the lanes, no second advanced plant from 'until it stands', and cancelling the engine queue on a list replacement keep it.
unread: Nothing torn or skipped; every tool ran. frames.py measures 'never started' from the command's site, and 16 of its 65 orders started at the engine's placed site 301-595 away (skipped, not items); 4 more were long walks or queued waits that then started, and 4 fell in the last 90 s (game end). never_started holds the 15 costliest of the 41 real ones; all 41 by cause: U2 5, U3 20, U4 1, U6 15 (the review lists the rest).
